title: Monetary Policy Report—April 2026
summary: The Bank of Canada held its target overnight rate steady at 2.25% amid rising uncertainty from the Middle East war and US tariffs. Inflation increased in March 2026 after holding near 2% for over a year, pushed higher by oil price increases from the Middle East conflict, and is expected to rise further in April before moderating toward the 2% target in early 2027. The Canadian economy continues adjusting to US tariffs with economic activity on a lower path than before tariffs were imposed.
key_points: Bank of Canada maintained target overnight rate at 2.25% (Bank Rate 2.5%, deposit rate 2.20%)
Inflation rose in March 2026 after being near 2% for over a year, driven by oil price increases from the Middle East war
Inflation expected to rise further in April 2026 before easing toward 2% in early 2027 as oil prices moderate
Canadian economic activity remains on a lower path due to US tariffs and trade uncertainty
Main risks: US trade relations and the Middle East war; inflation risks described as 'unusually high'
Average US tariff rates decreased recently but future of North America trade remains a key source of uncertainty
why_it_matters: This quarterly monetary policy report provides the Bank of Canada's comprehensive assessment of the Canadian economy. It signals the BoC is prioritizing uncertainty management over rate adjustments, holding rates steady despite inflation ticking higher. The outlook reflects dual headwinds from US trade restrictions and the Middle East conflict, both of which could force policy recalibration if inflation expectations become unanchored.
macro_context: The report identifies two major macro catalysts: US tariffs reshaping Canadian trade patterns (with steel and lumber exports declining significantly) and the Middle East war driving oil prices higher. The BoC projects inflation to spike temporarily in 2026 before moderating, while growth remains subdued. Global uncertainty has risen markedly per the report.
notes: Source is a high-tier official Bank of Canada publication. Contains the official rate decision embedded within the broader MPR. Governing Council members listed: Tiff Macklem, Carolyn Rogers, Toni Gravelle, Sharon Kozicki, Nicolas Vincent, Michelle Alexopoulos. Source is current (published today, 2026-04-29) with high confidence. No market structure content present.
